mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% in a month coincides with a 20-day positive S&P 500 forward return, as investors anticipate rate hikes and preemptively sell long-term equities.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in a given month
failure_condition: Over 60-day rolling window, 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during pre-inflation-surge periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly PAYEMS rises by more than 2% YoY, labor market strength is interpreted as a positive signal for corporate earnings prospects, driving a 60-day positive S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: Across 12 consecutive months with PAYEMS > +2% YoY, cumulative 60-day forward returns are not statistically outperforming the neutral baseline (M-W test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO of at least 5% signals weakening business capacity, which typically precedes a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investors reassess growth prospects.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month-over-month decline >= -5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In regimes with INDPRO declines >= -5% for two months, 20-day forward returns remain positive or flat over 90% of such events (empirical frequency > 80%).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly HOUST rises by more than 4% from the prior month, it reflects strong consumer demand, which is associated with a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as firms anticipate higher sales.
failure_condition: During 10 consecutive HOUST > +4% MoM events, the 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in FEDFUNDS for three consecutive months, below 1%, signals accommodative policy and typically precedes a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates rate-cutting expectations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS month-over-month decline for 3 consecutive months below 1%
failure_condition: During 15 such FEDFUNDS easing episodes, 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during pre-easing baselines (M-W test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4.5% for two consecutive months, the labor market softens, often leading to a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as investors price in weaker earnings.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE month-over-month decline for two consecutive months below 4.5%
failure_condition: Across 20 such UNRATE moderation episodes, 60-day forward returns remain positive or flat (empirical frequency < 20%).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in RSAFS of at least 10% in a month, accompanied by a parallel decline in GDPC1 of 5%, indicates weak demand and supply imbalance, which tends to produce a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS month-over-month change <= -10% AND GDPC1 month-over-month change <= -5%
failure_condition: In regimes with RSAFS <= -10% and GDPC1 <= -5% MoM, 20-day forward returns are not consistently negative (empirical frequency < 40%).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a tightening cycle is signaled by two consecutive months of FEDFUNDS above 5.25% and CPIAUCSL above 2.0%, which usually precedes a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate higher rates and slower growth.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS month-over-month > +5.25% AND CPIAUCSL month-over-month > +2.0% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During 10 such tightening regime signals, 60-day forward returns remain positive or flat (t-test p > 0.05).
